messages:
maya (oncall): noticing a big uptick in 5xx from hosted API around 14:06 UTC. p95 latency shot up and several customers opened tickets. spinning up war room.
liam (eng-sre): saw it too — error rate jumped to ~6.8% for /v1/generate. Grafana shard shows spike from 14:05-14:20.
sofia (support): reporting customers: AcmeAnalytics, Flownote. both seeing timeouts and 502s. customers are getting 504 gateway errors and retries are not helping.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-20260315-113. Severity: P1. Paging maya, liam, derek.
derek (runtime): initial look: several serving hosts returned 503 with logs containing "KV cache miss overload" and repeated "accept() failed: resource temporarily unavailable". Could be kernel accept queue exhaustion or connection storm.
maya (oncall): can you paste the exact log lines?
derek (runtime): here's a representative snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:06:12Z] model-serving-22 - ERROR - 503 ServiceUnavailable - AcceptQueue full - pid=4321 fd=1024
[2026-03-15T14:06:12Z] model-serving-22 - WARN  - KVCache miss rate 86% for model redwood-03-large
[2026-03-15T14:06:12Z] http-proxy     - ERROR - upstream returned 502 Bad Gateway
```
liam (eng-sre): also seeing spike in open file descriptors on those nodes. ulimit close to soft limit. autoscaler didn't spin up extra nodes. controller shows a backlog of pending pods for the model pool.
sofia (support): customers asking if this is an auth/billing issue — they reported 401 earlier but that may be separate. current main symptom: 504/gateway and timeouts.
maya (oncall): triage plan: 1) route traffic to healthy region/model variant 2) scale up serving pool manually 3) enable degraded-mode fallback to smaller quantized model 4) collect repro headers and sample request IDs.
liam (eng-sre): executing step 1: applying routing rule to shift 60% traffic from us-east-1 -> us-west-2 for affected model. patching policy now.
opsbot: Routing change applied: route-policy=emergency-1710567890 by liam. TTL=15m.
derek (runtime): scaling up pool: increasing replicas for redwood-03-large from 8 -> 18. K8s shows containers starting, but readiness probes failing on 3 nodes with "epoll_ctl: too many open files". suspect file descriptor leak in HTTP proxy sidecar.
liam (eng-sre): rolling restart of proxy sidecar on one affected node to reclaim fds.
sofia (support): passing updates to customers: "we've applied routing and are scaling; teams are investigating root cause — will follow up in 30m."
maya (oncall): mitigation check — error rate dropped to 1.2% after routing and partial scale-up. p95 latency back to normal for us-west-2. still some 5xx in us-east-1.
derek (runtime): temporary mitigation: enabled fallback route that serves from quantized variant redwood-03-q8 on overloaded hosts. applied with policy: max_latency_slo=1.2s.
liam (eng-sre): created a short-lived iptables limit to reduce new connections per-second to the proxy to protect accept() queue while we patch. Not ideal but buys time.
sofia (support): two customers confirmed recoveries: Flownote and AcmeAnalytics both report fewer 504s.
maya (oncall): next steps for warroom: - collect core dumps / strace on failing proxy instances - identify leak/holding fds - check autoscaler thresholds & controller metrics - validate fallback correctness for parity and costs
liam (eng-sre): assigning tasks: derek -> gather logs, strace and perf; maya -> coordinate with support and execs; ian (not in thread) -> review autoscaler thresholds; sofia -> compile customer timeline and tickets.
opsbot: Note: user 'ian' not in participants list; include if paging necessary.
derek (runtime): repro attempt: issued a burst test to emulate customer pattern (20 concurrent long-context requests per client). Observed rapid growth in connections and KV cache thrash; serving host respawned controller loop due to OOM in one replica. Here's the repro curl (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-03-large","input":"long context..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
liam (eng-sre): repro shows we exceed fd limit at ~120 concurrent clients. kube liveness restarts hide the problem.
maya (oncall): for immediate follow-up: open a postmortem doc, set action items, and schedule a joint debugging session tomorrow with runtime and infra.
sofia (support): adding ticket numbers and affected customers to the incident doc. Also recommending proactive outreach to top 10 customers who hit errors.
derek (runtime): root cause hypothesis so far: proxy sidecar has fd leak under connection storm + autoscaler didn't respond quickly due to conservative thresholds and pending pod scheduling delays. KV cache miss spike amplified CPU and memory pressure, causing restarts and 502s.
liam (eng-sre): short-term fixes we applied: routing to healthy region, manual scale-up, sidecar restart, iptables new-connection rate limit, fallback to quantized models.
maya (oncall): long-term action items (assign owners): "increase node ulimits and kube config for fd caps" - liam; "add sidecar e2e load test and memory/fd monitoring" - derek; "tune autoscaler to react to queue length + fd pressure" - ian; "postmortem with customer impact and cost analysis" - sofia.
sofia (support): customers want ETA on permanent fix. I'll send interim note saying engineering is targeting a patch in 48 hours and will provide weekly updates until resolved.
liam (eng-sre): also pushing a hotfix PR to proxy sidecar to close idle connections faster; will test in staging.
derek (runtime): attaching repro traces and sample logs to incident doc: INCIDENT-1710567890-logs.
opsbot: Incident severity downgraded to P2 at 14:52 UTC after sustained error rate <1.5% and majority of traffic routed away from impacted pool.
maya (oncall): thanks all. keep thread updated with any regression. we'll do full postmortem draft by EOD tomorrow.
sofia (support): will schedule customer follow-ups and include support notes about retry/backoff best practices.
liam (eng-sre): TL;DR for execs: transient connection storm + fd leak -> autoscaler lag -> 5xx/timeouts for hosted inference. mitigations applied; patch in progress. :white_check_mark:
